name: Anguilla
summary_text: Anguilla: own legal system; decriminalised 2019; very small, very quiet. Scored as a dependent jurisdiction: the parent framework governs what a visitor encounters, plus local society and enforcement. Score re-anchored 2026-09-24: United Kingdom (0.48) plus a local delta of -0.04. This jurisdiction was not covered by the dedicated state/province research passes.

sources.title: Judge rules Scottish guidance for housing trans prisoners is unlawful - BBC News
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: This BBC article is about Scotland's prison policy for trans prisoners (June 2026 ruling that guidance allowing some trans prisoners to be held in jails matching their gender identity is unlawful), not about Anguilla; it appears to have been included in the source list in error or as UK-context material.

sources.title: Suicide risk if trans prisoners are put in jails based on sex at birth, court told - BBC News
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: This BBC article is about the same Scottish prison-housing litigation (Feb 2026, suicide-risk arguments), not about Anguilla; included as UK-context material only.

sources.title: Gay Life in Anguilla - GlobalGayz
sources.claim_summary: GlobalGayz report (2012): 'Gay Life in Anguilla' - a quiet 35-square-mile island where homosexuality is virtually a non-issue: no visible community, organisations, Pride events or gay venues; gay life minimal and private; scattered gay-friendly hotel lounges exist.

sources.title: Anguilla Gay Weddings, Gay Wedding Venue in Anguilla, Gay Wedding in Anguilla
sources.claim_summary: Gay Destination Weddings travel page for Anguilla: markets the British island as a wedding/honeymoon destination with top beaches and a 'friendly, relaxed atmosphere' for same-sex couples.

AP via SodomyLaws (Jan 2001): Britain scrapped homosexuality laws in its five Caribbean territories (Anguilla, Cayman Islands, British Virgin Islands, Montserrat, Turks and Caicos) by Order in Council after local legislatures refused - decriminalising consensual same-sex acts in private; local religious leaders objected, calling it a cultural rift with Britain.

sources.title: My Queer Family Visited Anguilla—Here's What it Was Like - AFAR
sources.claim_summary: AFAR magazine (June 2023): first-person travel piece - a queer family visiting Anguilla openly ('out and proud on a tiny Caribbean island'); notes gay sex decriminalised since 2000 and explores whether LGBTQ travellers are welcome in practice.
